title: Mailbox rule and overtaking communications
summary: A properly invited acceptance may take effect on dispatch, while revocation ordinarily takes effect on receipt.
notes: The book traces the rule to Adams v. Lindsell and explains the dependable basis it gives the offeree. A medium not invited by the offer can change the result. Dispatch can also end the offeree’s power to reject, producing the problem of a rejection arriving before a previously mailed acceptance. The commentary raises estoppel where the offeror relies on the earlier-arriving rejection. The opening of U.S. Life v. Wilson is assigned, but its complete reasoning on the payment mechanism is not.
